Rashi on Arakhin 22a:10:1.hebrew: בתובעת כתובתה בב"ד - דכיון דשוב אין לה מזונות, לא מפסדי יתומים מידי בהמתנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:10:1.english: [The mishnah is speaking] of a woman who claims her marriage contract in court - For since she no longer has sustenance [from the estate], the orphans lose nothing by the waiting:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:11:1.hebrew: לא נזדקיק לה - לפרוע כתובתה, הואיל ומעכשיו אין מזונותיה על היתומים:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:11:1.english: We should not attend to her - to pay her marriage contract, since from now on her sustenance is no longer [a charge] upon the orphans:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:11:2.hebrew: כיון דאזדקקינן לה מעיקרא - בתחילת תביעת כתובתה, שיש בה להפסידה מזונותיה:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:11:2.english: Since we attended to her initially - at the beginning of her claim for her marriage contract, [a claim that] causes her to lose her sustenance:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:11:3.english: We attend to her in the end - to collect her marriage contract [for her]:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:16:1.hebrew: הא לא קשיא ר"מ היא דאמר כתובת [אשה] בבינונית - מיניה דידיה, כגון אם גירשה, גובה בבינונית, וקמ"ל ר"מ דמיתמי גובה בזיבורית:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:16:1.english: This is not difficult; it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir, who said that a woman's marriage contract [is collected] from intermediate[-quality land] - from [the husband] himself, for example if he divorced her, [she collects from intermediate land], and he teaches us that from orphans [she collects] from inferior[-quality land]:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:18:1.hebrew: כדשנין - כמו ששנינו למעלה בבעל חוב עובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:18:1.english: As we taught - [above], regarding a gentile creditor:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:20:1.hebrew: כשחייב מודה - בשעת מיתה הודה אביהם שעדיין לא פרע:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:20:1.english: Where the obligated party admits - At the time of his death, their father admitted [that he had not yet paid]:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:20:2.hebrew: כולהו נמי כשחייב מודה - מיירי ובעל חוב ישראל:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:20:2.english: All of them [are] also [where] the one obligated admits - and [they are dealing with] a Jewish creditor:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:21:1.hebrew: גרושה - אין לה מזונות מנכסי יתומים, ולכן אין נזקקין לנכסי יתומים בשבילה:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:21:1.english: A divorced woman - she has no right to sustenance [from the orphans' property, so the court should not attend to the orphans' property on her behalf]:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:23:1.hebrew: ההיא דרבי יוחנן - דאמר: כתובת אשה מגבינן מיתמי:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:23:1.english: That [statement] of Rabbi Yochanan - who said: We collect a woman's marriage contract [payment] from [the property of] orphans:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:23:2.hebrew: משום חינא מתנינן לה - כדי שימצאו האנשים חן בעיני הנשים, וינשאו להן. והלכך אפילו גרושה נמי:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:23:2.english: We learned it for the sake of favor - [This was enacted] so that men will find favor in the eyes of women and marry them. Therefore, [the same applies] even to a divorced woman as well:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:24:1.hebrew: בתר שיבקייהו - ימותו כאביהם שהניח להם ממון זה:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:24:1.english: After those who left them - they should die like their father, who left them this money:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:25:1.hebrew: לאו בני מיעבד מצוה נינהו - שאין לגבות מהם דקטנים הן, אלא ימתין עד שיגדילו:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:25:1.english: They are not [people] who perform a mitzvah - [One may not collect from them,] for they are minors; rather, [the creditor] should wait until they grow up:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:25:2.hebrew: צררי אתפסיה - אביהם נתן לבעל חובו מעות, או כסף וזהב, במשכון בשעת מיתה, ולא הספיק ליטול את השטר מידו:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:25:2.english: He gave him bundles as collateral - Their father gave his creditor coins, or silver and gold, as collateral at the time of his death, and did not manage to take the promissory note from his [the creditor's] hand:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:26:1.hebrew: דשמתיה - שנידוהו ב"ד לאביהן על שאינו פורע לזה חובו, ומת בשמתיה, דהשתא ליכא למיחש לצררי, דלא היה פורעו אלא בבית דין כדי שיתירו נידויו:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:26:1.english: That the court excommunicated him - the court excommunicated their father because he did not repay this [creditor] his debt, and he died in [a state of] excommunication. For now there is no need to worry about [the possibility that he paid with] bundles [of money, i.e., secretly], since he would not have paid him except in court, in order that they would lift his excommunication:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:27:1.hebrew: שלחו מתם בדשמתיה ומית בשמתיה - מיתוקמי כל הנך מתנייתא דלעיל דאמרו נזקקין:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:27:1.english: They sent from there: [where] he was excommunicated and died in his excommunication - All those mishnayot [and statements] above that say that [the court] collects [from orphans' property] are to be established [as referring to such a case]:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:27:2.hebrew: והלכתא כרב הונא - דהיכא דלא שמתוה, חייש לצררי:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:27:2.english: And the halakha is in accordance with Rav Huna - that where they did not excommunicate him [the father before his death], [the court] is concerned about [the possibility of] bundles [of money, i.e., that the debtor had already repaid the debt]:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:2:1.english: This halakha - [that was stated] by Rav Chisda:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:4:1.hebrew: קולפי טאבי - הכאות גדולות קבלתי על הדא שמעתא, שהיה מלמדיני אבימי שום היתומים לרבי מאיר שמכריזין ששים יום, והייתי מקשה לו: הא אמר ר"מ שלשים, והוא אמר לי: בא להכריז רצופין שלשים יום, בין יתומין בין הקדש:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:4:1.english: Kulfei tavi - Great blows [I received] on account of this halakha, for [Avimi] taught me that the appraisal of orphans' property, according to Rabbi Meir, [is proclaimed] sixty days, and I would challenge him: But Rabbi Meir said thirty! And he said to me: [It means] that if one comes to proclaim on consecutive days, [it is] thirty days, whether for orphans or for Hekdesh [consecrated property]:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:4:2.hebrew: ואם בא להכריז שני וחמישי - שהם ימי הדין, הוי השום ששים יום, וימי הכרזה שמונה עשר יום. צא וחשוב משני בשבת שמונה שבועות, הרי לך נ"ו ימים, ויהא בהם י"ו שני וחמישי; הוסיף עוד ארבעה ימים — שני ושלישי ורביעי וחמישי בשבת — הרי ס' יום משהתחיל ההכרזה, ויש בהן שמונה עשר ימי הכרזה:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:4:2.english: And if he came to proclaim [on] Mondays and Thursdays - which are the days of court sessions, the appraisal is [valid for] sixty days, and the days of proclamation are eighteen days. Go and count from Monday [for] eight weeks; that gives you fifty-six days, and among them there will be sixteen [days of] Monday [and] Thursday. If he added another four days — Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday — that is sixty days from when the proclamation began, and among them are eighteen days of proclamation:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:6:1.hebrew: אין נזקקין לנכסי יתומים - אין בית דין נזקקין למוכרן:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:6:1.english: The court does not attend to the property of orphans - [the court does not attend] to sell it:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:6:2.hebrew: רבית אוכלת בהן - שהיו מחוייבין לעובד כוכבים מעות ברבית:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:6:2.english: Interest consuming them - [This refers to a case] where [the orphans] were obligated to a gentile for money [that was owed] with interest:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:6:3.hebrew: משום מזוני - דכל זמן שאינה גובה כתובתה, נזונית משלהם של היתומים, והוי פסידא דידהו:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:6:3.english: Due to sustenance - For as long as she does not collect her marriage contract, she is sustained from their [the orphans'] property, and this is a loss for them:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:8:1.hebrew: אילימא בבעל חוב עובד כוכבים - שהוא דשקיל רבית, ולהכי נזקקין:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:8:1.english: If we say [that we are dealing] with a gentile creditor - who collects interest, and that is why [the court] attends [to the orphans' property]:

Rashi on Arakhin 22a:8:2.hebrew: מי צאית - עובד כוכבים להמתין ימי הכרזתינו בלא רבית:
Rashi on Arakhin 22a:8:2.english: Will he comply - [will a gentile creditor] wait for the days of our proclamation without [collecting] interest?

Tosafot on Arakhin 22a:24:1.hebrew: אמר רב נחמן מריש לא הוה מזקיקינן ליתמי כו' מכאן ואילך מזקיקינן כו' - והלכה כרב נחמן בדיני, דנזקקין לנכסי יתומים. והכי נמי איתא בהכותב (כתובות דף פד.), גבי הא דתנן: מי שמת והניח אשה ובעל חוב ויורשים, והיה לו מלוה או פקדון ביד אחרים — ינתן לכושל שבהם. ואמר ר' יוחנן עלה (שם): לכתובת אשה, משום חינא. אלמא, נזקקין:
Tosafot on Arakhin 22a:24:1.english: Rav Naḥman said: At first we would not attend to orphans, etc. From now on we attend, etc. - And the halakha follows Rav Naḥman in [cases of] law, that one attends to the property of orphans. And so too it is found in [the chapter] Hakotev (Ketubot 84a), regarding that which we learned in the Mishnah: One who died and left a wife, a creditor, and heirs, and he had a loan or a deposit in the hands of others — it is given to the weakest among them. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said about this (ibid.): [It is given] to the wife's marriage contract, because of [considerations of] grace. Evidently, one attends [to the property of orphans]:

Tosafot on Arakhin 22a:8:1.hebrew: תנן שום היתומים כו' במאי עסקינן אלימא בבעל חוב עובד כוכבים מי ציית - ואם תאמר: למה ליה לאותובי לרב אסי ממתניתין? ממילתיה דרב אסי גופיה הוה מצי למיפרך! דאמר דאין נזקקין לנכסי יתומים אלא אם כן רבית אוכלת בהם; במאי עסקינן האי דאין נזקקין? אילימא בבעל חוב עובד כוכבים, מי ציית להמתין עד שיגדילו? ואי בבעל חוב ישראל, מי שבקינן ליה דקאכיל רבית? וי"ל דממילתא דרב אסי לא מצי למיפרך, דאפשר לאוקמה בדלא תבע להו, ולעולם בב"ח עובד כוכבים איירי, ומש"ה אין נזקקין לנכסים לפרוע החוב אלא אם כן רבית אוכלת בהן [ואז] נזקקין אפי' לא תבע להו עובד כוכבים חובו, לפי שלא ירבה עליהן הרבית. אבל ממתניתין פריך שפיר, דודאי מדנחתי בית דין לשום בדתבע להו מיירי; לפיכך פריך: אי בבעל חוב עובד כוכבים, מי ציית עד אחר השלמת הכרזה שלא להרבות הרבית? ואי לא ציית, אם כן שמא יפסידו בהארכת הזמן יותר ממה שירויחו; דודאי אי לא ידעינן אי מרווחינן אי לא מרווחינן לא צריכי הכרזה, כדקאמר הש"ס בסמוך על מילתא דר' יוחנן:
Tosafot on Arakhin 22a:8:1.english: We learned: The appraisal of orphans, etc. What are we dealing with? If we say a gentile creditor, will he comply? - And if you say: Why did [the Gemara] need to challenge Rav Asi from the mishna? It could have refuted [him] from Rav Asi's own statement! For he said that one does not attend to the property of orphans unless interest is consuming it; [so] what are we dealing with, in this [case] where one does not attend [to it]? If we say a gentile creditor, will he comply with waiting until they grow up? And if a Jewish creditor, do we let him [collect], since he is consuming interest? And one can say that from Rav Asi's statement it could not refute, for it is possible to establish it [as a case] where [the creditor] did not demand [payment] from them, and in truth [Rav Asi] is speaking of a gentile creditor, and therefore one does not attend to the property to pay the debt unless interest is consuming it; [and] then one attends [to it] even if the gentile did not demand his debt from them, so that the interest on them will not increase. But from the mishna it challenges properly, for certainly, since the court went down to appraise, [the mishna] is speaking of [a creditor] who demanded [payment] from them; therefore it challenges: If it is a gentile creditor, will he comply until after the proclamation is completed, so as not to increase the interest? And if he does not comply, then perhaps they will lose through the extension of time more than they will gain; for certainly, if we do not know whether we are benefiting [them] or not benefiting [them], they do not need a proclamation, as the Gemara says shortly afterward regarding the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
